1.why: authorizedMfa() requires a valid session whose accountId matches the sole account and is invoked on every MFA endpoint, with no client-supplied account identifiers accepted.

2.why: Identity and OTP challenges are bound to the pending preauth record or session and the single account; the same code is not accepted for another user.

3.why: verify-enrollment enables MFA and stores the secret/codes but never deletes or rotates other existing session entries, so prior sessions remain valid.

4.why: The authenticator secret is stored with AES-GCM encryptAtRest and recovery codes are stored as argon2id hashes via strongHash.

5.why: Tokens, digits, recovery codes, and Base32 secrets are all produced with crypto.getRandomValues.

6.why: sid/preauth cookies are HttpOnly and the client never writes secrets/OTPs/tokens to localStorage, sessionStorage, or non-HttpOnly cookies.

7.why: Server validates email, phone, OTP, and recovery input with strict validators (isValidEmail/isValidPhone/isOtp/isRecovery) before use.

8.why: API responses are JSON and the UI builds the DOM with textContent/createTextNode, so untrusted values are not interpreted as markup.

9.why: The app performs no HTTP redirects at all, so an allow-list control is neither present nor violated.

10.why: headersFor() sets CSP, HSTS, X-Content-Type-Options, X-Frame-Options/frame-ancestors, and related secure headers on responses.

11.why: sessionCookie() and pendingCookie() set HttpOnly, Secure, and SameSite=Strict on all session/preauth cookies.

12.why: Errors are generic with no stack traces, and OTP seeds, backup codes, and session tokens are not written to server logs or URL query strings.

13.why: Pending identity codes and provisions are marked used and expire (CHALLENGE_MS); TOTP is time-step bound; recovery codes are removed after one successful use.

14.why: Sign-in, enrollment OTP, recovery, and pending-identity paths increment failure trackers and lock out after MAX_ATTEMPTS for LOCK_MS.

15.why: A new sid is issued on verify-identity, sessions enforce idle and absolute timeouts, and logout deletes the session and clears the cookie.
